I've refunded this game, and hopefully learned this lesson for the last time.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the PC port lacks native ultrawide support and has console-era frame rate limits.

citations.review_text:
Great game. Manages to be more free and open world than the previous entries in the series without you loosing interest like Odyssey or Valhalla. Good characters, decent missions and a beautiful map. Looking forward to playing the remastered version as well, as long as Ubisoft haven't botched it.

The only gripe I have with this game is that compared to my experience playing it on console, the performance isn't great. They didn't do a very good job with the port and it shows. This game runs less smoothly than AC1, and that's no exaggeration. Capped at 60fps and just feels a bit choppy.

Outside of that, this is a fantastic game.

Black Flag is still one of the best pirate games ever made. Unfortunately, the PC version has aged like milk.

No native ultrawide support. Console-era FPS locks. Basic PC features that should've been patched years ago are still missing.

"Just use mods," people say.

Yeah... about that.

The mods that fix ultrawide support and framerate limitations can completely break the game. Suddenly your inputs stop responding, scripted events refuse to trigger, and progression grinds to a halt. In my case, the very first assassination attempt on Edward never happened, leaving me stuck watching guards stare into space while the game waited for an event that would never fire.

So you're left choosing between:

Playing a compromised version with black bars and arbitrary FPS limits.
Playing a "fixed" version that might not even let you finish the tutorial.

It's hard to recommend a game that requires community patches just to feel like a proper PC release, only for those same patches to introduce game-breaking bugs.

Black Flag deserves better. The game itself is fantastic. This port isn't.

citations.review_text:
I really, really wanted to like this. I bought this when Skull & Bones was big, because the consensus was that this is the better pirate game experience, and I was looking for something to scratch that Uncharted Waters/Sid Meier's Pirates! itch. So I finally decided it was time to give it a try. The graphics feel a little dated while also being laggy, and I tweaked some settings to resolve the choppy framerate. I'm aware the new remake is out, and while I'm not willing to pay that much, I accept that this is going to show some wear around the edges.

Making the allowances for an older title, I want to say that the story so far is great, the challenges are enticing, the story is good and the characters are relatable. So why don't I recommend this? The controls are just awful, and just might make this otherwise-magnificent game entirely unplayable. I am playing over the Steam Link using my OG Steam Controller, and I don't think the controller itself is to blame. To run you have to hold down RT, fine. But to climb some surfaces you have to release RT, and others you have to press it again, and if you fail this unexplained combination of keys, your character decides to end his 15 point parkour challenge by leaping to his death from a tall building. Or I'm trying to sneak around behind an enemy to subdue him, but instead my guy doesn't slow down from his sprint and instead ends up circling the guy three times until his friend draws a sword and whacks me. Okay, a few times was hillarious. Then it became most times. Then the simplest parkour challenge ends up resetting because it didn't do what I thought I wanted, and I'm back to square one repeatedly, and it got unfun and eventually I ragequit. Ragequit in the first ten hours of the game on a non-soulslike feels wrong.

I'm gonna give it a bit more time and report back, but right now the controls are miserable. Maybe I'll try it with another controller or keyboard and mouse... But for now, my gameplay experience is not re…

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that certain missions, specifically tailing missions, are repetitive or show the engine's age.

citations.review_text: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag is one of the best games in the Assassin's Creed franchise. The game perfectly blends an engaging pirate adventure with the classic Assassin experience. Sailing across the Caribbean, exploring beautiful islands, hunting sea creatures, discovering hidden treasures, and engaging in epic naval battles never gets old. Edward Kenway is a charismatic protagonist whose journey from a selfish pirate to a true Assassin is well written. The world is massive, the soundtrack is memorable, and the naval combat is still among the best in gaming. While some tailing missions can be repetitive and the modern-day sections slow the pace, the overall experience is fantastic. Even years after its release, Black Flag remains a must-play for fans of open-world action games and pirate adventures. 10/10

Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag is the ultimate pirate fantasy. Whether you're hunting legendary ships, singing sea shanties with your crew, or exploring hidden islands, it's almost impossible not to have fun.

Edward Kenway is one of the franchise's best protagonists. Unlike previous Assassins, he begins as a selfish pirate chasing wealth and glory, making his journey toward understanding the Creed feel natural and rewarding. His character development is one of the strongest in the entire series.

Naval combat is the true star of the game. Upgrading the Jackdaw, battling enemy fleets, and taking down massive Man o' Wars never gets old. The open world is packed with things to discover, and sailing across the Caribbean while your crew sings is an experience few games can match.

The Assassin vs. Templar conflict sometimes takes a back seat to the pirate adventure, and some tailing missions can be frustrating. But those are small complaints in an otherwise outstanding game.

Black Flag isn't just one of the best Assassin's Creed games—it's one of the greatest pirate games ever made.

Rating: 10/10

"In a world without gold, we might've been heroes."

claims.claim: Reviewers note that exploring uncharted islands and swimming back to the boat becomes tedious when trying to collect items or achievements.

citations.review_text: I decided to play through the game on PC, after the remake, and the original has held up quite well. The game still has breathtaking visuals, and you are able to stealthily navigate the environment. The combat is straight forward, and the story is captivating. The most annoying thing I have found about this game is exploring uncharted islands, then swimming back to the boat. This isn't necessary to beat the game, but when trying for 100% achievements it's become tedious.

Edward is an amazing character. A true pirate. His character arc is rather interesting, and is one I consider to be, at best, rushed. You'd have to play the game and form your own opinion, but aside from that character arc the story is great and the naval combat fulfilled a huge itch I've had for some time. Albeit the way Ubisoft hid the collectibles in various small islets made it rather tedious to get them all.

YouTube Black Flag Multiplayer Lvl 55:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xCEUQGNaJgI&t=161s

Assassin’s Creed IV Black Flag:

Is easily one of the best Assassin’s Creed games, and honestly one of the best pirate games ever made.

The story follows Edward Kenway during the Golden Age of Piracy, and the Caribbean setting is amazing. Sailing across the ocean, upgrading the Jackdaw, hunting ships, exploring islands, diving for treasure, and getting pulled into the Assassin and Templar conflict all works so well together. It feels like a pirate game first and an Assassin’s Creed game second, and that is a big reason why it stands out.

The gameplay loop is addictive. You can do main missions, naval battles, forts, ship upgrades, hunting, collectables, underwater areas, and side activities without it feeling boring. The music and sea shanties also add so much atmosphere that even just sailing around can feel relaxing and fun.

The story, characters, combat, world, and exploration are all great. Edward is a strong main character, and the game does a great job making his journey feel meaningful. Going for 100% completion is mostly fun, although it can still get grindy in places, especially if you are clearing everything on the map.

I would recommend Assassin’s Creed IV Black Flag to almost anyone. Fans of the series, casual players, story players, pirate fans, and achievement hunters should all give it a try.

This is not just a good Assassin’s Creed game. It is a must-play.

citations.review_text:
This game is fantastic, with a tragic tale, awesome combat and naval gameplay, beautiful open world and full of fun activities. Only complaint is there are a lot of eavesdropping missions which are very annoying, other than that this game is a blast. The ending hit me this time and made me felt a bit emotional, very good story.

Freedom Cry DLC is okay, there are lot of tailing missions in the middle that are annoying, other than that the missions are good and game has a cool story. The naval combat is awesome and the naval missions are the better one's in this DLC. Adewale as a character is bit flat though the DLC is mostly entertaining and fun throughout it's run. A decent additional content to the base game.

Multiplayer starts off good and playing on different maps and modes for the first time feels great, but after a while the repetition kicks in it feels like a chore, if they had kept the grind up-to level 30 or closer would have been fine, but level 55 feels like it takes eternity to get there. Took me 30 hours of grind to do all Multiplayer achievements, definitely not worth the effort.

Had a blast with the base game, enjoyed the Adewale DLC and had a somewhat miserable time with very grindy Multiplayer!! Cheers Ahoy!
Interesting historical context, good graphics especially on the sea, absorbing plot. Following targets is a bit tedious.
